quotes.quote: Weight those rates by the different case mixes actually assigned. The assistant’s total becomes fifty-four percent, while control reaches seventy-six. quotes.quote: In general, binary harm cannot exceed either control success or assistant failure, so its maximum is the smaller of those two rates.

In a chain, assignment changes a diagnostic summary, which affects resolution. Conditioning on that mediator blocks this directed route. A total effect includes that route, so adjusting it away changes the comparison.

In a fork, a pre-treatment common cause influences assignment and outcome. Conditioning on that cause blocks this particular backdoor path. In a collider, two arrows meet at a common effect. The path is blocked until we condition on that effect or one of its descendants; other non-colliders can still block a longer path.

answers.reason: Adjusting only for C blocks A←C→Y, preserves A→M→Y, and leaves the collider K unconditioned.

quotes.quote: Under independent tickets, fixed target weights and conditional binomial sampling, estimate variance by summing squared stratum weights times the two cell variances.

quotes.quote: Give each assistant ticket one divided by its assignment probability, and each control ticket one divided by one minus that probability. These are assignment probabilities, not success predictions.
A weight-only concentration diagnostic squares the sum of weights and divides by the sum of squared individual weights.

quotes.quote: If the true policy always routes a target group to the assistant, its control probability is zero. That is a structural positivity failure for a comparison requiring control there. Weighting cannot create its missing outcome.

An empty finite-sample cell alone does not prove structural impossibility. In a new ten-ticket batch with independent assistant probability point nine, the chance all ten receive assistant is point nine to the tenth, about thirty-four point nine percent. The control cell is empty in that event even though the true control probability is positive.

answers.reason: P has positive control probability 0.2, so its empty control cell can occur by chance. Q has zero control probability, creating structural support failure.

quotes.quote: The Wald ratio divides the outcome difference between instrument groups by their workflow-uptake difference.

With the instrument assumptions and monotonicity, the population ratio identifies the average effect on compliers, whose workflow changes from control to assistant when encouraged. Monotonicity rules out defiers; it does not require everyone to follow the flag.

answers.reason: Wald effect = (66%−60%)/(60%−20%) = 0.15, or 15 points. Under the supplied assumptions it identifies the complier effect; the uptake increase gives a 40% complier proportion.

quotes.quote: Doubly robust evaluation starts with the reward model’s target-policy prediction for each context. Add the target-to-logging probability ratio times the difference between the observed reward and its prediction for the observed action. Then average those corrected values.
A multi-step agent changes its later state distribution when earlier choices change. A trajectory importance weight can multiply the target-to-logging action ratios across time.
A sequential doubly robust estimator includes future value and per-step corrections; the one-step immediate-reward formula is not automatically an estimator for a whole agent return.

answers.reason: Trajectory weight = 3×0.25 = 0.75. Evaluating the sequential return requires the future-value and per-step corrections described in the narration.

quotes.quote: Consider a separate example where both workflows resolve half their tickets. Audit every assistant ticket and every failed control ticket. In the audit log, assistant cases retain successes and failures, while control cases contain only failures. Selection creates an apparent assistant advantage from equal underlying rates.

The audit is a common effect of assignment and outcome. Conditioning on it opens a selection path in the assumed graph. The direction of the resulting bias depends on the audit rule, so recording the mechanism matters more than applying a general slogan about which variables to control.

Verified as definitions and conditional mechanisms. Consistency is Y=Y(A). A stochastic workflow can include random draws in its specified mechanism; consistency does not require identical generated text. Meaningful workflow changes require corresponding treatment-version definitions. Shared staffing can make a ticket’s outcome depend on other assignments, requiring a broader potential-outcome definition. Offering access and assigning actual use define different interventions. Treatment-version issues are addressed by [VanderWeele and Hernán](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4219328/); resource competition explicitly appears in [Rosenbaum and Rubin, §1.1](https://www.stat.cmu.edu/~ryantibs/journalclub/rosenbaum_1983.pdf). Verified. A conditioned non-collider blocks a chain or fork; a collider ceases to block when it or a descendant is conditioned on. Another conditioned non-collider can still block the same longer path. These rules match [Pearl’s d-separation definition](https://bayes.cs.ucla.edu/BOOK-2K/d-sep.html). The causal Markov assumption licenses independence from d-separation; faithfulness supplies the reverse implication. Open paths need not yield nonzero associations because effects can cancel. Conditioning on a mediator does not automatically identify a direct effect. These qualifications agree with [Pearl’s overview](https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r350.pdf).

Adjustment uses Σz P(Y|A=a,Z=z)P(Z=z), with the same population weights for both arms. An unblocked hidden-tier path is not removed by increasing sample size.
